root_cause.text: The workqueue type was set to IDXD_WQT_NONE prematurely in idxd_wq_disable_cleanup() and idxd_drv_disable_wq() before resource deallocation functions completed, causing other driver code to incorrectly interpret the workqueue as empty and skip necessary cleanup operations, resulting in memory leaks.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the `wq->type = IDXD_WQT_NONE;` assignment from idxd_wq_disable_cleanup() (line 385) and idxd_drv_disable_wq() (line 1561) to the end of idxd_wq_free_resources() (line 178), ensuring the type is only set to NONE after all resource deallocation (free_descs, dma_free_coherent, sbitmap_queue_free) is complete. The commit message explicitly states that setting wq type to NONE signals to other driver parts that "the wq is empty (all its resources were released)," indicating that premature type assignment was causing resource cleanup to be skipped.

This prevents other driver code from prematurely interpreting the workqueue as empty and skipping necessary cleanup operations, which was the core issue causing memory leaks.

This group removes a redundant workqueue type reset that is already handled by memset. However, the vulnerability root cause is about the workqueue type being set to IDXD_WQT_NONE PREMATURELY before resource deallocation completes. Removing a redundant reset does not address the timing/ordering issue that causes other driver code to misinterpret the workqueue state during cleanup. The fix should focus on reordering when the type is cleared relative to resource deallocation, not on eliminating redundant resets.
